geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the existing occupied mass with a courtyard logic to create a legible public void without destroying the compact primary mass.
Set a moderate courtyard margin so the void is usable and visible in plan and elevation.
Orient the courtyard opening toward the access side to repair the missing active edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the current corner-cut threshold with a true courtyard/void gesture so the frontage can read as a public ground condition rather than a sealed object.
Size the void generously enough to be legible as usable public space.
Open the public void toward the verified access side in the program frame so the ground response aligns with the frontage condition.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact object in all four views, so the base mass is stable, but it fails the neighborhood-living brief because the ground relationship is sealed and the blue access edge is not answered by a legible public void, entry seam, or undercut. The orange mass is also a highly repetitive toothed/stepped crown with no meaningful section logic; it feels like a sculpted extrusion rather than a capacity-aware mixed-use building. The parcel is respected in outline, but the dominant gesture simply sits inside it rather than forming an active threshold or courtyard figure. Repair integrity is strong because the mass is uninterrupted and not visibly self-colliding, but program fit is weak due to the missing active street edge and the absence of a public ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is far more compact and object-like; it does not yet express the tower/slab scale or vertical public sequence of the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Use a single legible mass with a controlled taper/step profile and a clear urban threshold rather than fragmented volumes.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is too tall and context-specific to copy directly; the candidate lacks the same section-driven vertical continuity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A crisp vertical profile can carry hierarchy if the base remains clearly grounded and the upper form resolves as one continuous section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a low retail/cafe object; the candidate is a more centralized compact mass and does not share its frontage logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A small building can still read as program-appropriate when it has a clear public corner or threshold and a simple primary body.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not achieve the same strong court or sectional promenade; the stepped object here is more sealed and less spatially legible.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A courtyard/void can organize neighborhood scale by connecting public ground and upper mass into one continuous section.

warnings: The silhouette is coherent, but coherence alone is not enough here because the access edge remains unarticulated.
The stepped crown reads as an arbitrary surface condition rather than a program-bearing section.
A future revision should preserve the compact primary body while carving a clearer public threshold on the verified frontage side.
